questions.q: If a 9-digit number $897359y7x$ is divisible by $72$, then what is the value of $(3x + 4y)$ for the largest possible value of $y$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $54$

Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisibility of 72 ka sidha matlab $8$ aur $9$. Exam word 'largest $y$' diya hai toh trial top se shuru karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Largest $y$ lena hai toh seedha $9$ se check maar rule of 8 ke liye. Phir digit sum nikal ke rule of 9 lagana.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Assume } y=9 \implies 97x / 8 \implies x=6 \\ \text{Sum for 9:} \, 48 + 6 + 9 = 63 \text{ (Divisible)} \\ (3(6) + 4(9)) = 18 + 36 = 54 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Hamesha last 3 digits rule apply karke dependent variable $x$ ka ek chota set banana padta hai for different values of $y$.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{If } y \text{ is max, try } 9: \frac{97x}{8} = 121 \text{ R } 4+x \implies x=6 \\ \text{Checking sum} \pmod 9: \frac{48+y+x}{9} = \frac{63}{9} = 7 \text{ (Valid)} $$

TCS Trap: TCS yahan variable restriction me khelta hai. Tum minimum wala solve kar loge and option me answer bhi hoga but galat ho jayega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Hamesha bold trap words jaise 'largest' ya 'smallest' possible value pe gaur karo, pura khel wahi badalta hai.

questions.q: If the 6-digit number $51x34y$ is divisible by 72, find the value of $(2x + 3y)$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
$72 = 8 \times 9$. Sabse pehle 8 ka rule last 3 digits pe lagega, phir digital sum 9 ke liye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, 8 ke rule me $34y$ hai. 300 series me 344 8 se kat-ta hai (yaad rakhna $8 \times 43$). Toh seedha $y=4$.
Ab 9 ke liye CPR mat laga, bas Digital Sum (C9 method) kaat de: $5+4=9$ (cancel), $1+3+4+x = 8+x$. Isko 9 banne ke liye $x=1$ chahiye.
Find: $2(1) + 3(4) = 2 + 12 = 14$. Khatam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Digital sum is universally the best approach for 9. Just ignore combinations that add up to 9.

Future Exam Takeaway:
88, 72, 99 wale questions SSC ke damad hain, humesha 8, 9, 11 ke separate rules apply karo.

questions.q: If $N = 77^{77^{77}}$ and $M = 33^{33^{33}}$, what is the unit digit of $N \times M$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Cyclicity of 4)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... power towers dekh ke ghabrana nahi hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Base digits $7$ aur $3$ hain. Unki power towers ajeeb lag rahi hain but essentially wo Odd numbers ki Odd power hain. Matalab power HAMESHA Odd hi rahegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Unit digit me sirf aakhri power $4$ se divide hoti hai.
$N$ me power $77^{\text{odd}}$. $77 \pmod 4 \equiv 1$. Toh $1^{\text{odd}} = 1$. Base power $1$ aayegi. $7^1 = 7$.
$M$ me power $33^{\text{odd}}$. $33 \pmod 4 \equiv 1$. Toh $1^{\text{odd}} = 1$. Base power $1$. $3^1 = 3$.
Unit digit = $7 \times 3 = 21 \implies 1$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Power tower $a^{b^c}$ me bas $b \pmod 4$ check kar liya karo aur uski power $c$ chala do.

Future Exam Takeaway: Power towers dekh ke ghabrana nahi, Modulo 4 Cyclicity hamesha bachayegi.

questions.q: If a 9-digit number $32x4115y2$, is divisible by $88$, then the value of $(4x-y)$ for the minimum possible value of $y$ is?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $88$ divisibility hamesha $8$ aur $11$ ke combined rules se todi jaati hai. Minimum $y$ nikal ke directly $11$ ki equation me fit karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, pehle $8$ ka rule (last 3 digits): $5y2$. Minimum $y$ pucha hai. $y=0$ rakha toh $502$ fail. $y=1$ rakha toh $512$ (jo $8$ ka cube hai) perfectly pass! Toh $y=1$ lock ho gaya.
Ab $11$ ka rule lagao (Alternating sum difference):
Odd places: $3+x+1+5+2 = 11+x$.
Even places: $2+4+1+y = 7+y$.
Difference: $(11+x) - (7+y) = 4 + x - y$.
$y=1$ yahan daal do: $4 + x - 1 = 3 + x$.
Ab isko ya toh $0$ banna hai ya $11$. Positive digits ke lie $0$ impossible hai, toh $11$ banao. $3 + x = 11 \implies x = 8$.
Humein pucha hai: $4x - y = 4(8) - 1 = 32 - 1 = 31$. Option D is right.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Isolate divisibility rules strictly. The parameter 'minimum' simplifies the search space for $y$ instantly, converting a two-variable Diophantine problem into a linear one.

Future Exam Takeaway: 'Minimum possible' aur 'Maximum possible' limits hamesha dhyan se padhna, warna correct variables aakar bhi final value galat ho sakti hai.

questions.q: What is the remainder of $71^{382}$ divided by 100?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Base ka unit digit 1 hai. Aakhiri do digits nikalne ka shortcut yahi kehta hai ki unit place par humesha 1 hi aayega. Options dekh, sirf pehle option me 1 hai. Dekhte hi tick!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, in case options close hon, Ninja Technique lagana:
1. Unit digit hamesha 1.
2. Tens digit $\implies$ Base ki tens digit (7) $\times$ Power ki unit digit (2). $7 \times 2 = 14$. Iska last digit 4 utha le.
Dono mila ke ban gaye 41.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Ye actual me Binomial theorem ka expansion hai: $(70+1)^{382}$. First all terms will end with 00 except the last two which give $382 \times 70 \times 1 + 1 = 26740 + 1$, ending in 41.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Base ending in 1 ka hamesha Tens(Base) * Unit(Power) wala shortcut use karna.

questions.q: How many two-digit prime numbers are there between $10$ to $100$ which remain prime numbers when the order of their digits is reversed?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Static GK of Math)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Number system ke static facts sidhe memory se aate hain, prove nahi karne baithna.

Pen-Free Observation: Reverse karne par $2, 4, 5, 6, 8$ end me aane wale numbers even ya div by $5$ ban jate hain. Toh sirf $1, 3, 7, 9$ combinations matter karenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Wo primes list karo: $11, 13 (31), 17 (71), 37 (73), 79 (97)$.
Dhyan rakhna $19$ prime hai but ulta hoke $91$ banta hai jo $13 \times 7$ hota hai, toh wo out ho jayega.
Total count: $11, 13, 17, 31, 37, 71, 73, 79, 97$. Exact $9$ prime numbers hain.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Memory based check, specific digits ending logic reduce combinations.

Future Exam Takeaway: Kuch chize exam me prove nahi karni hoti, unhe as a static data treat karo.

questions.q: Find a positive integer less than 55 that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 5, and a remainder of 7 when divided by 11.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Options ko dhyan se dekh bhai. Number ko 5 se bhag dene par 3 remainder bachna chahiye, matlab unit digit ya toh 3 hoga ya 8. Saare options ke end me 8 hai, toh direct 11 ki divisibility test kar!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bina pen uthaye! Number $11k + 7$ ki form mein hoga. Seedha options ko 11 se divide kar aur dekh kis me 7 bachta hai. 18 ko 11 se bhag doge, 7 remainder aayega. 28 me 6 aayega. Baaki ud gaye, sirf Option 1 pass!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) ka basic laga. Let Number $N = 11k + 7$. Ab $k=1$ rakh ke dekh: $N = 18$. Ab 18 ko 5 se divide kar, remainder 3 aaya. Condition satisfied.

Future Exam Takeaway: Hamesha bade divisor ka base form banao aur options me hit & trial lagao, CGL me seconds bachenge!

questions.q: On dividing the numbers 6453 and 1676 by a three digit number M, the same remainder is obtained. Then, find the sum of the digits of the number M.
questions.s:
Answer is 11.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab bhi 'same remainder' ka case ho, HCF/Difference method kaam aata hai. Dono numbers ka difference le lo, wo M ka exact multiple hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Difference $= 6453 - 1676 = 4777$.
Number M (3-digit) is 4777 ka factor hona chahiye. 4777 kisse divide hota hai? Prime test kar: 17 se try kar.
$4777 = 17 \times 281$.
Since M ek 3-digit number hai, M strictly 281 hoga.
Sum of digits of $M = 2 + 8 + 1 = 11$.

questions.q: If $A = 0.497$, $B = 0.299$ and $C = 0.157$, then what is the value of $(A+B+C)$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Decimals ko exact solve karna time wastage hai. Digital Sum (C9 Method) aur Unit Digit hack lagao options nikalne ke liye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
sbke upon me 1000 so num ka unit digit dekh ke add kardo opt matched. Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Sabse pehle C9 (Digital Sum) check kar.
$A = 0.497 \implies 4+9+7 = 20 \implies 2$
$B = 0.299 \implies 2+9+9 = 20 \implies 2$
$C = 0.157 \implies 1+5+7 = 13 \implies 4$
Expression ka total C9 Sum = $2 + 2 + 4 = 8$.
Ab Options check kar kiska digit sum 8 hai:
911/1000 $\implies 9+1+1 = 11 \implies 2$
93/100 $\implies 9+3 = 12 \implies 3$
953/1000 $\implies 9+5+3 = 17 \implies 8$ (Bhai match ho gaya!)
Khatam sawaal!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Last digit Unit Trick bhi lagti: $7 + 9 + 7 = 23$, yaani sum ke end mein 3 aana chahiye. 953 me 3 hai. Direct add karna $0.497+0.299+0.157 = 0.953$ fraction me $953/1000$ banta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Decimal additions/fractions dekh ke darna mat, Digital Sum lagakar options jaldi eliminate karo.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $(1^{49} + 2^{49} + 3^{49} + \dots + 49^{49})$ is divided by 50?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Symmetry Grouping)

Dekh bhai... Itni badi series add hone ke liye nahi bani hoti, ye sirf pairs mein cutne ke liye hoti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Algebraic symmetric grouping. Formula yaad kar: $(a^n + b^n)$ hamesha $(a+b)$ se divide hota hai agar $n$ odd ho.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
First aur last term pakdo: $1^{49} + 49^{49}$. Sum of bases $1+49 = 50$. Toh yeh 50 se divisible hai.
Aise hi $2+48$, $3+47$ sab pairs zero remainder ban jayenge.
Beech mein sirf ek bichara bachega: $25^{49}$ kyunki iska pair nahi hai.
$25^n$ ko $50$ se divide karo toh remainder hamesha 25 aata hai (for any $n \ge 1$). Ans is 25.

Future Exam Takeaway: In massive series, look for first and last term symmetry to collapse the series into zero remainders.

questions.q: The non-terminating repeating decimal among the following fractions is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Base Properties)

Dekh bhai... fraction ko evaluate nahi karna, sirf denominator ke DNA ko padhna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Fraction tabhi terminate hota hai jab uske denominator ke prime factors sirf 2, 5, ya dono hon ($2^n \times 5^m$).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Option B dekh, $76 = 4 \times 19$.
Isme prime number 19 aa gaya, jo fraction ko non-terminating bana dega kyunki numerator 679 bhi 19 se completely divide nahi hota. Direct hack!

Future Exam Takeaway: Hunt for primes other than 2 and 5 in the denominator to instantly spot non-terminating fractions.

questions.q: What are the last two digits of $4^{4^4}$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $96$

Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Power tower with base 4. Bada number hai but trick $76$ par hinge kar rahi hogi kyuki numbers terminating trick wahi rehti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Convert base aur power into 2. Iske baad powers ko $10$ me break karke seedha 76 magic number exploit karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ 4^{256} = (2^2)^{256} = 2^{512} \\ 2^{512} = 2^{12} \times (2^{10})^{50} = 4096 \times (1024)^{\text{Even}} \\ \text{Mod } 100: 96 \times 76 \equiv 96 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $2^{10} = 1024$. Iski agar Even power karein toh aakhri do digit hamesha $76$ aate hain aur odd karein to $24$ aate hain.

Mathematically :-

$$ (1024)^{\text{Even}} \equiv 76 \pmod{100} \\ 4096 \equiv 96 \pmod{100} \\ 96 \times 76 = 7296 \equiv 96 \pmod{100} $$

TCS Trap: Bacche isko $4^{256}$ karke uske aage expand karne ke raste dhundhne lag jate hain jo possible nahi hai in raw digits without $2$ based hacks.

Exam Takeaway:

> Magic property yaad kar bhai: Any number ending in $76$ jab kisi bhi power of 2 se multiply hota hai, toh answer ki last 2 digits original number ke end digits hi rehti hai (yahan $96$).

questions.q: How many numbers are there between $99$ and $1000$ such that the digit $8$, occupies the unit's place?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Range 99-1000 exactly 3-digit array define karti hai. Positions fix karke directly possibilities multiplier maar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Teen box bana digits ke liye. Last me sirf ek possibility ($8$) fix. First digit 0 nahi ho sakti (1 se 9). Second (middle) digit pe koi rok nai ($0$ se $9$). Multiply maar de.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Box } [H][T][U] \\ \text{Places count} \implies (9 \text{ opts}) \times (10 \text{ opts}) \times (1 \text{ opt fix } 8) \\ = 9 \times 10 \times 1 = 90 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Arithmetic progression bana ke total terms formuli se mapping karte hain basic level pe.

Mathematically :-

$$ AP = 108, 118, 128 \dots 998 \\ L = a + (n-1)d \\ 998 = 108 + (n-1)10 \\ 890 = 10(n-1) \implies n = 90 $$

TCS Trap: Arithmetic approach me log limits lene (first term) me phaste hain. Permutation places concept limits eliminate kar deta hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Digits placement constraints wale array count questions mostly Permutations (places fix multi) se solve hone chahiye AP series se nahi.

questions.q: In how many ways can the number $11025$ be resolved into two factors which are co-prime to each other?
questions.s:
Final Output: $4$

Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Number chota ho ya bada, co-prime factor pairs hamesha base primes ki counting par nikalte hain. Factorize fast.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Number ka prime factorization maar. Dekh kitne distinct prime numbers aaye. Fir seedha formula thok de $2^{n-1}$.

Mathematically :-

$$ 11025 = 3^2 \times 5^2 \times 7^2 \\ \text{Distinct primes } (n) = 3 \\ \text{Ways} = 2^{n-1} = 2^{3-1} = 4 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Co-prime hone ka matlab do numbers me kuch common na aye. Toh prime powers ek saath ek side jani chaiye.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = p_1^a p_2^b p_3^c \dots \\ \text{Co-prime factors} = 2^{k-1} \text{ where } k \text{ is number of distinct prime bases.} $$

TCS Trap: Yahan factor powers ko consider karke calculation lamba matt karna, co-prime pairs sirf distinct primes ginte hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Direct hack yaad rakh: Co-prime factor pairs hamesha $2^{n-1}$ hote hain jahan $n$ distinct primes ka count hota hai.

questions.q: Find the smallest integer which should be added to the given expression to make it a perfect square? $79998 \times 79999$
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekhte hi algebraic identity $n(n+1)$ dikhni chahiye. Multiply karne ka paap nahi karna hai!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Let $n = 79998$. Expression is $n \times (n+1) = n^2 + n$.
Isme kya add karein ki agla perfect square $(n+1)^2$ ban jaye?
$(n+1)^2 = n^2 + 2n + 1$.
Hamare paas $(n^2 + n)$ hai, toh humein $(n + 1)$ aur chahiye.
Matlab $79998 + 1 = 79999$ add karna padega!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
General rule: Product of two consecutive integers $n(n+1)$. Add the larger number $(n+1)$ to make it $(n+1)^2$. Subtract the smaller number $n$ to make it $n^2$.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Seedha formula yaad rakh: $A \times (A+1)$ me BADA number add karne pe perfect square banta hai, aur CHHOTA number subtract karne pe.

questions.q: What is the remainder when the $7$-digit number $4538291$ is divided by $101$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $58$

Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor $101$ dikhte hi samajh ja $10^2+1$ ka case hai. Isme pichhe se $2-2$ ke block ban ke plus-minus khela jata hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Right side se $2$ digits ke pairs pakad. Alternating plus aur minus maar. Jo value bachi, wahi seedha remainder hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Blocks: } 04, 53, 82, 91 \\ \text{Alt Sum} = 91 - 82 + 53 - 04 = 58 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraic divisibility rule lagta hai yahan. Agar base $100$ hai toh $100 \equiv -1 \pmod{101}$.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = a_0 + a_1(10^2) + a_2(10^4) + \dots \\ N \pmod{101} \equiv a_0 - a_1 + a_2 - a_3 \dots $$

TCS Trap: Students left side (starting digits) se block banana shuru kar dete hain aur fas jate hain. Block hamesha unit digit se start karna hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Base $10^2+1$ (like $101$) requires alternating blocks of $2$. Base $10^3+1$ (like $1001$) requires blocks of $3$.

Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Series Splitting)

Bhai, dhyan se dekh! Yeh do mixed telescoping series ka jhol hai. Ek flow mein add karne gaya toh fass jayega.

Pen-Free Observation: Isko 7 aur 11 wale numerators mein alag-alag split kar le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Series 1: $7 \times (1/2 + 1/6 + 1/12 + \dots + 1/156) = 7 \times (1 - 1/13) = 84/13$.
Series 2: $11 \times (1/3 + 1/15 + \dots + 1/575)$. Yahan difference 2 ka hai denominators ke factors mein ($1\times3, 3\times5$), so formula lagega $\frac{1}{\text{diff}} \times (\text{first} - \text{last})$. $11 \times \frac{1}{2} \times (1 - 1/25) = 132/25$.
Dono ko jod de: $84/13 + 132/25 = 3816/325$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Mixed series are CGL mains traps designed to induce panic; separate them to reveal standard telescoping patterns.

questions.q: Find the last two digits of $3^{1000} \times 7^{1000}$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Jab exponents same ho, bases multiply kar. Jaise hi base end in $1$ (matlab 21) aayega, wahi puraani 'X1' wali jugad fix kar de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Combine the bases directly. Base 21 mil gaya. Tens place ke liye base tens ko power unit se multiply, and unit is obviously 1.

Mathematically :-

$$ (3 \times 7)^{1000} = 21^{1000} \\ \text{Unit digit} = 1 \\ \text{Tens digit} = (2 \times 0) \pmod{10} = 0 \\ \text{Result} = 01 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Using binomial expansion of form $(10x + 1)^n$, which expands to end with $(nx \pmod{10})1$.

Mathematically :-

$$ (20+1)^{1000} = \dots + {1000 \choose 1}(20)^1(1)^{999} + 1 \\ 20000 + 1 \implies \text{Last two are } 01 $$

TCS Trap: $3$ ka cyclicity alag, aur $7$ ka cyclicity alag nikalne beth jaoge toh multiplication me last two digits bura fasa dengi.

Exam Takeaway:

> Exponent rules apply first: $a^n \times b^n = (ab)^n$. Fir $(\dots X1)^Y$ wali solid tens trick apply karo.

questions.q: If 83 is divided successively by 7, 3, and 2, then what are the successive remainders?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Successive division normal division se alag hai. Yahan agle step ka dividend pichle step ka quotient (bhagfal) ban jata hai. Step by step follow karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Step 1: Pehle 83 ko 7 se divide kar. $83 = 7 \times 11 + 6$. (Quotient = 11, Pehla remainder = 6). Option B aur D gaye!
Step 2: Ab pichle quotient (11) ko next divisor (3) se bhag de. $11 = 3 \times 3 + 2$. (Quotient = 3, Dusra remainder = 2).
Step 3: Ab naye quotient (3) ko next divisor (2) se bhag de. $3 = 2 \times 1 + 1$. (Teesra remainder = 1).
Successive remainders line se aaye: 6, 2, 1. Option A mark kar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
In successive division, number $N = d_1 \times q_1 + r_1$. Then $q_1 = d_2 \times q_2 + r_2$, and so on. Remainders flow consecutively exactly as derived.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division me kabhi bhi original number (83) ko saare divisors se baar baar bhag mat dena, woh normal division hota hai.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $15^{400}$ is divided by $1309$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $1$

Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Itna bada divisor bina logic ke nahi aata. Ye chote prime numbers ka product hai, seedha Chinese Remainder Theorem lagana hai idhar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Divisor ko primes me tod. Unke respect me modulo theorem check kar. Sabme value $1$ aayegi toh final remainder bhi wahi hoga.

Mathematically :-

$$ 1309 = 7 \times 11 \times 17 \\ 15^{400} \pmod 7 \equiv (15^6)^{\dots} \equiv 1 \\ 15^{400} \pmod{11} \equiv (15^{10})^{\dots} \equiv 1 \\ 15^{400} \pmod{17} \equiv (15^{16})^{\dots} \equiv 1 \\ R = 1 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fermat's Little theorem ko component basis par split karke lagana hai yahan pe.

Mathematically :-

$$ a^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod p \\ x \equiv 1 \pmod{p_1}, x \equiv 1 \pmod{p_2} \implies x \equiv 1 \pmod{p_1p_2} $$

TCS Trap: Bade weird numbers ko direct expand/modulo property marne chale jate hain bina primes todhe. Hamesha divisor ko break karo.

Exam Takeaway:

> Large weird divisors are always product of primes. Break them and conquer.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $7^{99}$ is divided by $344$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Negative Remainder Concept)

Dekh bhai, powers bade ho toh divisor ke aas-paas base ki power dhundhni chahiye, taaki remainder $+1$ ya $-1$ ban jaye.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor $344$ hai. $7$ ki powers yaad kar: $7^1=7$, $7^2=49$, $7^3=343$. $343$, $344$ se bas $1$ chota hai! Boom!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$7^{99} = (7^3)^{33} = (343)^{33}$.
Ab $343 \div 344$ ka remainder $-1$ aata hai.
$(-1)^{33} = -1$. Negative remainder allow nahi hota math me, toh isme divisor add kar do.
Real Remainder = $344 - 1 = 343$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Hamesha power ko aise split karo ki base, divisor ke $\pm 1$ range mein aa jaye. Arithmetic ki cycle bohot fast chalti hai is format pe.

questions.q: How many factors of $N = 2^7 \times 3^4 \times 5^3$ are both even and perfect squares?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Perfect square ke liye powers even honi chahiye (0, 2, 4...). Aur 'Even' factor maanga hai, toh base 2 ki power me 0 nahi aa sakta! Waha se filtering karni hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Base 2: Powers available 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Perfect square & even hone ke liye choices hain $2^2, 2^4, 2^6$ (Total 3 choices).
Base 3: Powers available 0,1,2,3,4. Perfect square ke liye choices $3^0, 3^2, 3^4$ (Total 3 choices).
Base 5: Powers available 0,1,2,3. Perfect square ke liye choices $5^0, 5^2$ (Total 2 choices).
Total factors = $3 \times 3 \times 2 = 18$.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Jo condition question de, bas uske hisab se un base powers ko count karke P&C ka basic multiplication rule laga do.

questions.q: $N$ is a natural number less than $1000$ and is a multiple of $5$. When $N$ is successively divided by $7$ and $8$, it leaves remainders of $2$ and $3$ respectively. How many possible values of $N$ exist?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change

Dekh bhai, successive division me seedha 'base building' equation banani hoti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisors $7, 8$ ke remainders $2, 3$. Final divisor $7 \times 8 = 56$ banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Find the least number: $8 \times 0 + 3 = 3$. Then $3 \times 7 + 2 = 23$. So general form is $N = 56k + 23$.
Hume pata hai $N$ multiple of $5$ hai. Is equation me mod $5$ lagao: $N \equiv 1k + 3 \equiv 0 \pmod 5 \implies k = 2$.
First valid number: Put $k=2 \implies 56(2) + 23 = 135$.
Next numbers will have a gap of LCM(56, 5) = $280$. So numbers are $135, 135+280=415, 695, 975$.
Total $4$ values less than $1000$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division equation banake, dusri condition (multiple of 5) ke liye usko wahi mod kar diya karo, pura solve karne me time bachega.

questions.q: A book contains $500$ pages. How many times does the digit $3$ appear in the page numbers?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Block Counting Method)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... frequency counting hamesha blocks me karni chahiye.

Pen-Free Observation: Digit occurrence fixed pattern me chalti hai. Har $100$ ke block me tens aur unit digit ki fixed frequency milti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Har standard block ($0-99, 100-199$ etc) me kisi bhi digit ka count exactly $20$ hota hai (in tens & unit places).
Range $1$ se $500$ me total $5$ block banenge. Toh $5 \times 20 = 100$ bar $3$ aayega.
Ab dhyan de 'Hundreds place' par: $300$ se leke $399$ tak, pure $100$ bar lagatar $3$ aayega.
Total jodd do: $100 + 100 = 200$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base value calculate karke specific zone ke extra instances add karo.

Future Exam Takeaway: Digit frequency $0-99$ block me hamesha $20$ bar hoti hai, ye fact rat lo, calculation fast ho jayegi.

Answer is 414.

Pen-Free Observation: Even numbers ki simple AP (Arithmetic Progression) series hai. First term aur last term pata hai, toh $\frac{n}{2} (a+l)$ lagana best hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Number of terms $n = \frac{\text{Last} - \text{First}}{\text{Difference}} + 1 = \frac{40 - 6}{2} + 1 = 17 + 1 = 18$ terms.
Sum = $\frac{n}{2} \times (a + l) = \frac{18}{2} \times (6 + 40) = 9 \times 46$.
Unit digit check: $9 \times 6 = 54$, aakhri digit 4 aayega. Options me 424, 400, 414 hain. $9 \times 46 = 414$ direct leap. JSM/Deviation lagane ki zaroorat nahi yahan!
